::: {.callout-note .part-overview icon=false}
## Why this part comes here

Negotiation turns private judgment into joint choice. The sequence moves from basic architecture to distributive preparation and tactics, then to integrative trade-offs and advanced agreement design.
:::

## Guiding questions

- What is my alternative and walk-away point?
- How should anchors and concessions be managed?
- How can differences in priorities, beliefs, and risk create value?

## Chapters

- **Chapter 30:** [Negotiation Is Joint Decision-Making](../chapters/30-negotiation-is-joint-decision-making.qmd) — Interdependence turns choice into a shared search — About 19 min
- **Chapter 31:** [Preparing to Claim Value](../chapters/31-preparing-to-claim-value.qmd) — BATNA, reservation value, targets, and the zone of possible agreement — About 14 min
- **Chapter 32:** [Anchors, Concessions, and Bargaining Tactics](../chapters/32-anchors-concessions-and-bargaining-tactics.qmd) — Claiming value without losing learning, reputation, or the deal — About 21 min
- **Chapter 33:** [Interests, Priorities, and Trade-Offs](../chapters/33-interests-priorities-and-trade-offs.qmd) — Creating value before dividing it — About 16 min
- **Chapter 34:** [MESOs, Contingent Contracts, and Better Agreements](../chapters/34-mesos-contingent-contracts-and-better-agreements.qmd) — Learning priorities, betting on differences, and improving implementation — About 22 min

## Bridge to the next part

The final part asks how these skills can be embedded in recurring organizational and personal decision systems.
